_README: PreToolUse guard — SHIPPED OFF, AND THIS FILE IS WHY IT IS A SEPARATE FILE.
Claude Code never reads this file. It is a paste-able example, nothing more.
TO ENABLE: copy the "PreToolUse" key below into the "hooks" object of
.claude/settings.json, then restart your session. Read what it does first:
tools/guard_pretooluse.py --selftest    # 33 behavioural cases, no Claude Code needed
tools/README.md                         # what it guards and why it asks rather than denies
WHY NOT AN INERT KEY IN settings.json. It used to ship as "_DISABLED_PreToolUse"
in the real settings file — JSON has no comments, so an inert key looked like the
idiom, and it sat in the file you already had rather than an example nobody opens.
That bet depended on Claude Code ignoring unknown hook events silently. It stopped:
the key now produces `hooks._DISABLED_PreToolUse: Unknown hook event ... was ignored`
on EVERY session start, in EVERY project, forever, with nothing an adopter could do
about it (#101). The first question it drew was "is this due to the AI scaffold?" —
a deliberately-disabled feature is indistinguishable from a broken config to the
person reading the warning, and that channel also carries genuinely broken settings.
A no-op "PreToolUse" entry would have been worse: it registers a real hook that runs
on every tool call to do nothing, trading a visible warning for an invisible cost.
The enable step is still one edit, and a fresh project starts with a clean console.
THE COMMAND LOOKS FOR THE GUARD; IT DOES NOT ASSUME YOUR CWD IS THE REPO.
It was `python3 tools/guard_pretooluse.py`, resolved against the session's working
directory. On 2026-08-09 that was measured to be the wrong assumption on this
project's own machine, where sessions open in the PARENT of three scaffold repos —
the layout this scaffold's own AGENTS.md prescribes. Every other cwd-relative hook
had therefore never fired once. For a journal that is a lost feature; for a SECURITY
GUARD it is worse than not installing it, because you believe you are covered.
So it takes the first tools/guard_pretooluse.py it finds in the working directory or
one level below, and execs it. Every copy is identical — scaffold_upgrade.sh
force-installs tools/ — so which one runs does not matter; the guard reads the target
path out of the hook payload, not out of its own location.
If it finds none it exits 0 and allows, which is the same fail-open rule the guard
itself follows: ai/SECURITY.md, containment over prevention.
TWO GUARDS, BOTH OFF, AND THEY ARE SEPARATE ENTRIES ON PURPOSE.
guard_pretooluse.py enforces the SECURITY hard lines — destructive commands,
protected paths, commits on main. guard_delegation.py is a WORKING-HABIT nudge:
it interrupts the first large write to a delegatable file when the local model has
not drafted anything recently. Enable them independently; most projects want the
first and only some want the second.
guard_delegation asks rather than denies, once per file per session, and then
allows. Set "delegation": {"guard": {"decision": "deny"}} in
ai/localcoder.config.json once your project has decided that drafting is the norm.
tools/guard_delegation.py --selftest    # 24 cases, half of them known-good input

hooks.command: bash -c 'r="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}"; if [ -f "$r/ai/STANDARDS.md" ]; then set -- "$r"; else set -- . */; fi; for d in "$@"; do [ -x "$d/tools/guard_pretooluse.py" ] && exec python3 "$d/tools/guard_pretooluse.py"; done; exit 0'

bash -c 'r="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}"; if [ -f "$r/ai/STANDARDS.md" ]; then set -- "$r"; else set -- . */; fi; for d in "$@"; do [ -x "$d/tools/guard_delegation.py" ] && exec python3 "$d/tools/guard_delegation.py"; done; exit 0'
